slides.texte_overlay:
weird psychology tricks
that actually work

the open palms

show your palms when you talk, especially when you're explaining something. open hands read as honest and relaxed, and people trust what you say a little more.

the curious silence

when someone finishes talking, wait two seconds before replying. people very often add the most honest part of their thought in that small, quiet gap of silence.

the fact effect

spend 5 minutes a day learning one surprising fact. people instinctively trust and listen to someone who seems calm and well informed, without you ever showing off.

the fact effect

slides.texte_overlay:
the walking talk

have hard conversations side by side on a walk, not face to face across a table. walking together quietly makes people more open and far less defensive.

the small favour

ask someone for a small favour, like borrowing a pen. people tend to like you more after helping you, because their brain quietly decides you must be worth it.
